interview.hardest_part: Efficiently managing the turn-based loop through screenshots alone — knowing which tiles/cities to click, queuing production and research, and moving builders/units without losing track of the map and menus across many turns within a 3-hour wall-clock limit.
interview.likely_failure: Falling behind on tech/production timing, accumulating era score/amenities problems, or inability to precisely navigate the UI to place districts and buildings before the clock runs out; also early Aztec positioning may lack coastal/desert resources needed for certain techs and districts like Harbor.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Turn-based play waits for input, tech tree lists all Ancient/Classical techs clearly for queuing, Aztec builder ability to boost district construction speeds early infrastructure, standard rules make milestone requirements known, one AI opponent on Prince is manageable, and science victory focus rewards a wide tech beeline.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Screenshot-only control makes multi-step actions error-prone, 3-hour real-time limit constrains deep optimization, unassisted production/research choices can waste turns, districts and buildings require specific city-planning and population thresholds, one AI opponent can still threaten or out-settle if ignored, and only one attempt means an early mistake is costly.
